title: Computational strategies for copy number variation detection; disease association; and beyond.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the supplementary bundle (2.8 MB zip). Additional file 2 (Table S1) is one sheet, 132 rows x 7 columns: a bibliography of CNV (copy number variation) association studies (Authors, Year, Title, Platform, Journal, Cited By, DOI). The other files are two Word documents and figure images.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Data availability statement says this is a review with no new primary data; its figures reuse Collins et al. Table S3 (disease-associated CNV loci) and Harris et al. Supplementary Information 2. Neither was evaluated here because both belong to other papers.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads freely, but it holds only a literature table and Word documents (checked the files).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no measured outcome. Table S1 lists 132 publications with metadata; nothing in it is a prediction target (checked the file).

a3_inputs_present.note: No genomic or phenotypic features: the columns are only bibliographic fields (checked the file).

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: there are no measurements.

a5_enough_rows.note: 131 study rows plus a header row, and they are citations rather than samples (counted in the file).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Matches the paper's description of Table S1 as a list of CNV association studies.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists to trace back to a measurement.

honest_claim_h3: None: this is a review article with no primary dataset to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use CNV (copy number variation, i.e. gained or lost DNA segments) study metadata to predict disease association. Not feasible: no outcome data exists here.
plain_idea.train_on: Only a 131-row list of published CNV association studies with bibliographic fields; no genotypes or phenotypes.
plain_idea.predict: Nothing measurable. The table holds no outcome, only citations.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Not worthwhile from this paper. The underlying resources it cites (Collins et al. disease-associated CNV loci) would need their own evaluation.

ml_idea: None viable. At most this review points to other datasets, such as Collins et al.'s table of disease-associated CNV loci, which would need to be evaluated as separate candidates.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no modelling task.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open Table S1. Done: it is a 131-row bibliography with no outcome column.

verdict_reason: This is a review article with no new data. Its only table is a 131-row bibliography of CNV association studies with no features or labels (checked the file).
